issues.description: Endpoint path mismatch for the Persons API: the problem statement and the client code use the path "/persons" (the exercise specification requires POST /persons, GET /persons, PUT /persons/{personId}, DELETE /persons/{personId>}), but the server implementation in the solution repository exposes the endpoints under "/people" (e.g. @GetMapping("people"), @PostMapping("people"), etc.). This creates a breaking structural inconsistency: client requests to /persons will not be handled by the server in the solution, and students following the problem statement to implement /persons will disagree with the provided server solution. The template PersonResource is still a TODO, so students will implement endpoints according to the problem statement (/persons) but the solution server uses /people, causing confusion when comparing to the reference solution and preventing end-to-end behavior if the client and server paths are not aligned.
issues.suggested_fix: Unify the endpoint paths across specification, template, client and server. The simplest fix preserving the problem statement is to change the server mappings from "people" to "persons": replace @GetMapping("people"), @PostMapping("people"), @PutMapping("people/{personId}"), @DeleteMapping("people/{personId}") with @GetMapping("persons"), @PostMapping("persons"), @PutMapping("persons/{personId}"), @DeleteMapping("persons/{personId}"). Alternatively, change the problem statement and client code to use "people" — but keep all three artifacts consistent. Update tests/documentation to match the chosen path.

issues.description: REST resource naming mismatch for the same conceptual entity (persons). The problem statement specifies endpoints under /persons (e.g. POST /persons, GET /persons, PUT /persons/{personId}, DELETE /persons/{personId}). The client implementation (solution) sends requests to /persons. However, the server implementation (solution) exposes the persons endpoints under /people (e.g. @GetMapping("people"), @PostMapping("people"), etc.). This creates a direct mapping/functional mismatch: students following the problem statement or client code will expect /persons endpoints, but the server listens on /people. The inconsistency exists across artifacts (problem statement vs. solution server) and even within the solution repository (client uses /persons while server uses /people), causing runtime failures and strong student confusion about which path is correct.
issues.suggested_fix:
Make the resource path name consistent across all artifacts. Preferred minimal fixes:
- Rename the server endpoints from "people" to "persons" (change @GetMapping("people"), @PostMapping("people"), @PutMapping("people/{personId}"), @DeleteMapping("people/{personId}") to the corresponding "persons" paths) so they match the problem statement and the client requests. OR
- Alternatively, if you prefer "people", update the problem statement and all client code to use /people consistently. Ensure both client and server use the same path name so students can map the problem description to the template and solution without confusion.
